subject: Acquire split compiler analysis only when the final WVB is missing
claim: The finished split WVB is validated before intermediate analysis or symbols are acquired. The cache sentinel reproduced two unnecessary analyzer invocations with the old coordinator after intermediate eviction; the revised coordinator restores the same product without either invocation and rejects corrupt final evidence before construction. Cache/verifier edits select the focused split owner, whose four checks include fourteen cache cases and exact optimized/complete compiler byte oracles.

source.value: Worktree based on 062ec88a; exact changed implementation and routing identities are recorded in the Windows run inputs.

runs.target: Regression diagnosis against coordinator from 062ec88a: an emission hit incorrectly reconstructed symbols and analysis after their checkpoint families were evicted
runs.command: node Tools/Native/Test-Cached-Split-Project-Wvb.mjs (new sentinel against unchanged 062ec88a coordinator, before implementation edit)

runs.target: Changed-file gate; focused split owner 5107 ms, 31 general and 282 native routing cases, documentation checks

runs.host: Debian under WSL, Node 20.19.2, repository on /mnt/d/windvale/dev01
runs.target: Four focused split-owner checks, including fourteen cache cases and exact 308-byte optimized and 395-byte complete pruning outputs

limitations: The first failed run is the intended regression diagnosis; it is not passing verification of the old coordinator.

The source closure, producer identities, host namespace, final product digest, and analysis request key still bind each hit; cached intermediate files are not dependencies of an already completed product.
The fourteen cache cases use bounded instrumented producers to prove invocation, invalidation, cleanup, and corruption behavior. They do not time a compiler-scale analysis rebuild.
Reported elapsed times are single focused observations with retained bootstrap tools and fresh test fixtures; peak memory was not measured.

A read-only attempt to locate a reusable current compiler-analysis product found that the retained historical checkpoint keys did not match current sources. No speculative cold compiler build was started.

The owner duration profile remains the conservative 300-second estimate. Before routing correction, a cache-test-only edit selected runner reconstruction plus the focused owner at 1200 expected seconds; that over-budget plan was not executed.

Complete compiler preparation, runner reconstruction, production admission, and paired-host full qualification were not run. This is development evidence and does not establish the seconds/minutes targets for those broader workloads.
